access noun

a way in; the right or chance to reach or use

also access to, have access, way in, admission, accessible

classical

Gell. 16.5.3: per quem ā viā aditus accessusque ad aedīs est
Ov. Rem. 120: difficilēs aditūs

aditus, aditūs m.

noun, fourth declension

access, approach; the right to approach

Other words

  • accessus, accessūs m. — an approach, access

    noun, fourth declension · also used · classical · Gell. 16.5.3: aditus accessusque

  • admissiō, admissiōnis f. — admission to see an important person, an audience

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Sen. Ben. 6.33.4: prīmae et secundae admissiōnēs (Lewis & Short); M-O s.v. available: access (to an important or busy person)

  • cōpiam facere — give access to, make available

    also used · classical · Ter. Ph. 113: sibi ut ejus faciat cōpiam

    See available.

Examples

  • locum ante jānuam domūs vacuum, per quem ā viā aditus accessusque ad aedīs est

    the open space in front of the door of a house, through which there is access from the street to the houseGell. 16.5.3

  • dum furor in cursū est, currentī cēde furōrī; difficilēs aditūs impetus omnis habet

    while the rage is running, give way to it as it runs: every outburst is hard to get nearOv. Rem. 119–120

See also available, full access, read access, permission, enter.

SourcesLewis & Short: aditus · Lewis & Short: accessus · Lewis & Short: admissio · Lewis & Short: copia

Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. available: access (to an important or busy person).
